the properties of the connections of pyramidal cells in neocortex.
the properties of synaptic connections between pyramidal and spiny interneuronal cells in the neocortex of the adult rat.
the functional properties of the excitatory connections between pyramidal neurons and interneurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pyramidal axons are not only capable of making connections onto interneurons but they do so in a manner that can be considered a "typical" axon terminal.

pyramidal cells make a wide variety of synaptic connections onto spiny interneuron cell somata, dendrites and spines, and that these connections have properties that are distinct from those onto pyramidal cell dendrites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the properties of the synapse between pyramidal neurons and spiny interneuron are similar in many respects to those of the synapse onto pyramidal neurons, with the exception that the former are characterized by low release probability.
pyramidal axons make a wide range of connections onto spiny inhibitory neurons, with the probability and kinetics of transmitter release varying with presynaptic firing pattern.

in rat somatomotor neocortex the major excitatory input onto pyramidal cells arises from the dendrites of other pyramidal neurons, and the major excitatory synaptic input onto inhibitory interneurones arises from the axons of pyramidal neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there are two types of excitatory synapse onto interneurons in the neocortex, one from local axon collaterates, the other from long-range axons, and that these synapses differ markedly in the way in which presynaptic spike frequency and pattern of firing modulate release probability.
there is a novel, and important, class of excitatory connections in cortex that is not synaptically organized.
the probability of transmitter release at synapses onto inhibitory interneuron targets is low and that the properties of these synapses differ from those of synapses onto pyramidal neurons.
